problem: Parallelizing code for irregular data structures (sparse graphs, unbalanced trees, non-uniform meshes) is notoriously hard, and LLMs fail catastrophically, generating code with race conditions, deadlocks, and poor scaling.
approach: ParEVO synthesizes high-performance parallel algorithms via a Critic-Refine pipeline that generates 13,820 tasks, specialized fine-tuned models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Gemini) on ParlayLib semantics, and an Evolutionary Coding Agent that repairs correctness using compiler and profiler feedback.
contribution: On the ParEval benchmark, ParEVO achieves 107x average speedup and 13.6x speedup on complex irregular graph problems, outperforming GPT-5-Thinking and Gemini-3-Pro while matching expert human-written baselines.

problem: Dueling optimization (using only comparison oracles) has been studied mainly in unconstrained Euclidean spaces, leaving important applications on Riemannian manifolds unsolved.
approach: Proposes Riemannian Dueling Normalized Gradient Descent (RDNGD) and a projection-free Riemannian Dueling Frank–Wolfe (RDFW) method, establishing iteration complexity bounds for geodesically smooth or convex objectives.
contribution: Extends dueling optimization to Riemannian manifolds with theoretical iteration and oracle complexity guarantees, validated on synthetic and real applications.

problem: Many physical systems are inherently chaotic and uncertain, yet dominant PDE modeling approaches rely on deterministic predictions, and retraining probabilistic models from scratch is computationally expensive.
approach: Retrofits pre-trained deterministic models into probabilistic ones via the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) proper scoring rule, maintaining architecture agnosticity with minimal code changes.
contribution: Achieves 20–54% reductions in rollout CRPS and up to 30% improvements in variance-normalized RMSE on single-system models, and 40% improvement in CRPS on PDE foundation models, with modest additional training cost.

problem: Obtaining accurate Zeroth-Order Hessian estimation with low variance remains challenging in high dimensions for derivative-free methods like bilevel optimization and Bayesian inference.
approach: ZoVH reinterprets ZO Hessian approximation through the lens of single-step Policy Optimization, unifying classical estimators via baseline selection and employing query reuse for sample efficiency.
contribution: Provides unbiased Hessian estimators with variance optimality guarantees and establishes convergence guarantees for the resulting curvature-aware ZO algorithm, validated empirically.

problem: Modern language models reason within bounded context windows, a fundamental constraint that limits long-horizon reasoning capabilities.
approach: Proposes recursive models where the model can recursively invoke itself to solve subtasks in isolated contexts, proving that any computable problem admits a recursive decomposition requiring exponentially smaller active context per subtask.
contribution: Trains a 3B model to reason recursively on Boolean satisfiability, significantly outperforming frontier LLMs on tasks requiring long-horizon combinatorial search.

problem: Deepfakes have achieved near-perfect semantic realism with forensic traces only in subtle structural anomalies, and single-view approaches fail to generalize due to dominant semantic features overwhelming subtle artifact cues.
approach: DiCoME employs Geometric View Purification to decompose representations into decorrelated semantic and artifact views, then leverages Uncertainty-Aware Evidential Learning to synthesize these views by explicitly modeling epistemic conflict.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing deepfake detection approaches in generalization and provides calibrated uncertainty estimates for trustworthy detection.

problem: Current VLA models lack reasoning capability, real-time status monitoring, and self-correction abilities during embodied manipulation tasks.
approach: Sentinel-VLA introduces an active sentinel module to monitor execution status and trigger dynamic reasoning only when necessary (during planning or error detection), paired with Self-Evolving Continual Learning and Orthogonal Continual Adapter to prevent catastrophic forgetting.
contribution: Boosts task success rate by over 30% compared to SOTA model PI0, with all training data (2.6 million transitions across 44 tasks) automatically generated via a designed pipeline.

problem: Video reward models for text-to-video generation are impractical due to their large parameter size and prohibitive memory costs, yet image reward models are misaligned with temporal objectives.
approach: VELR employs ensemble latent reward models that predict rewards in latent space via VAE, bypassing expensive backpropagation through VAE decoders and full video reward models, with ensemble techniques for uncertainty quantification.
contribution: Reduces memory by up to 150GB (12.4% of standard ReFL memory) while maintaining comparable performance to standard ReFL, enabling efficient video RM-based reinforcement learning at previously unattainable scales.

problem: LLMs deployed as agents use general-purpose tokenizers designed for broad language, leading to inefficient tokenization of repetitive tool-calling patterns that dominate agentic interactions.
approach: AgentVocab derives specialized vocabulary entries from real tool-calling traces and adapts the model vocabulary to reflect structural and semantic regularities without task-specific schema engineering.
contribution: Preserves tool-calling performance while reducing latency by 17.7% and 19.5% on τ-bench and τ²-bench respectively, with seamless integration into standard agent pipelines.

problem: Existing approaches for inferring gene regulatory networks from perturbational datasets fail to capture non-linear dynamics of biological processes such as cellular differentiation.
approach: PerturbODE employs interpretable neural ODEs to model cell state trajectories under perturbations, deriving the causal GRN from neural ODE parameters via a single-hidden-layer feedforward network that groups genes into interpretable co-regulated modules.
contribution: Demonstrates efficacy in GRN inference and perturbation response prediction across simulated and real overexpression datasets.

problem: Releasing differentially private parameters of geodesic regression (which models data on Riemannian manifolds) requires privacy protection, but privacy mechanisms for non-Euclidean spaces are under-developed.
approach: Applies the K-Norm Gradient mechanism to Riemannian manifolds, deriving sensitivity bounds tied to Jacobi fields and space curvature.
contribution: Demonstrates methodology on spheres, symmetric positive definite matrices, and Kendall's planar shape space with privacy guarantees generalizable to any Riemannian manifold.

problem: Deploying lightweight models in dynamic edge environments requires retraining whenever device resource constraints change, resulting in excessive computational overhead.
approach: DFMPQ trains a weight-sharing mixed-precision supernet via federated learning representing diverse bit-width configurations, using semantic-aware training and sensitivity-guided greedy search to satisfy heterogeneous resource constraints without additional optimization.
contribution: Achieves competitive accuracy with significantly reduced computational cost, enabling retraining-free deployment for dynamic edge computing environments.

problem: Low-bit model quantization for image super-resolution causes accuracy degradation due to activation quantization error, which is harder to minimize than weight quantization error.
approach: CondiQuant formulates activation quantization error via the condition number of weight metrics and designs an efficient proximal gradient descent algorithm to jointly minimize condition number while maintaining output.
contribution: Outperforms existing post-training quantization methods without computation overhead and achieves theoretically optimal compression ratio in model parameters.

problem: Current segmentation models encode entire images before focusing on specific objects, wasting computational resources on irrelevant regions.
approach: FLIP (Fovea-Like Input Patching) selectively samples multi-resolution patches centered on objects of interest, allocating high-resolution processing to object centers while maintaining coarser peripheral context via biologically-inspired top-down attention.
contribution: With 440× fewer parameters than SAM2-L (0.51M vs 224.45M), FLIP-Tiny reaches 79.90% mean IoU vs SAM2-L's 75.87%, and FLIP-Large achieves 83.26% IoU while running 2× faster than SAM2-L.

problem: Depth estimation for transparent objects fails because RGB-based cues are unreliable in regions affected by refraction and light transmission.
approach: PolarDepth incorporates both RGB and polarization inputs (DoLP and AoLP) and embeds polarization-derived physical priors (refractive index, zenith angle, azimuth angle) into an implicit geometric representation to constrain depth inference.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in transparent object depth estimation; introduces PTOD dataset with synchronized RGB, polarization, and depth data.

problem: Bayesian inference is limited by challenges of prior and likelihood elicitation; practitioners leverage foundation transformers like TabPFN but require epistemic uncertainty for scientific estimands not directly parameterized by the model.
approach: TabMGP builds a martingale posterior on TabPFN for tabular data, replacing prior/likelihood requirements with a predictive rule and focusing inference on parameters defined through a loss function.
contribution: Produces credible sets with near-nominal coverage and outperforms both handcrafted MGP constructions and standard Bayesian baselines.

problem: Multimodal learning must align modality-specific representations while suppressing modality-dependent noise and redundancy, but existing IB methods rely on restrictive distributional assumptions.
approach: IBMA enforces the Information Bottleneck principle for both fused and modality-specific representations via modality-specific alignment and introduces a distribution-free variational upper bound avoiding unrealistic latent feature assumptions.
contribution: Achieves superior multimodal learning performance compared to existing methods, validating the effectiveness of modality-specific representation alignment.

problem: Existing brain modeling approaches treat encoding and decoding as isolated tasks, relying on unimodal alignment and overlooking the brain's intrinsic multimodal integration nature.
approach: BrainJanus proposes a Unified Brain Tokenizer to quantize neural dynamics into discrete tokens aligned with visual and linguistic representations in a shared Omni space, with an All-in-One autoregressive architecture enabling any-to-any generation (image-to-brain, text-to-brain, brain-to-image, brain-to-text).
contribution: Achieves superior performance across diverse benchmarks with zero-shot generalization and preserves interpretable biological topography.

problem: Text-to-Image ReID retrieves visible pedestrian images, but in low-light or nighttime settings, visible images lack identity details while infrared images capture contours and textures effectively.
approach: Proposes Text-to-Visible-Infrared ReID (TVI-ReID) task with Semantic Decoupling Learning to form color-related and color-irrelevant feature subspaces and Semantic Distribution Transfer to adapt text-visible pretraining to text-infrared matching.
contribution: Outperforms existing SOTA TI-ReID methods on tri-modal datasets designed to test the new TVI-ReID task.

problem: RL for diffusion models optimizes an objective (DDPO) different from pretraining objectives (score/flow matching), leading to variance increase and slow convergence.
approach: Reveals DDPO as implicit score/flow matching with noisy targets; proposes Advantage Weighted Matching (AWM) that reweights each sample by its advantage while keeping the modeling objective identical to pretraining.
contribution: On GenEval, OCR, and PickScore benchmarks, AWM delivers up to 34× speedup over Flow-GRPO when applied to Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and FLUX without compromising generation quality.

problem: Programmatic policies are claimed to generalize better than neural policies in RL benchmarks, but much of this gap may arise from uncontrolled experimental factors rather than representational reasons.
approach: Re-evaluates three core benchmarks (TORCS, Karel, Parking) by training neural policies with modifications (sparse observations, cautious intrinsic rewards) to match programmatic policy training conditions.
contribution: Shows that neural policies can match or exceed OOD generalization of programmatic policies when trained fairly, advancing understanding of representational factors in generalization.

problem: Parallel diffusion decoding suffers from flip-flop oscillations where tokens are remasked and restored unchanged, slowing inference and consuming revision budgets.
approach: COVER (Cache Override Verification for Efficient Revision) performs leave-one-out verification and stable drafting via KV cache override, with stability-aware seed prioritization that balances uncertainty, downstream influence, and cache drift.
contribution: Markedly reduces unnecessary revisions and yields faster decoding while preserving output quality on diverse benchmarks.

problem: Process reward models allow fine-grained credit assignment, seemingly contrasting with outcome reward models, but the relationship between them has been unclear.
approach: Proves that GRPO with an outcome reward model is equivalent to a PRM-aware RL objective with a Monte-Carlo-based PRM; identifies a flaw in GRPO that hinders exploration/exploitation under imbalanced steps/rewards and proposes λ-GRPO to mitigate it.
contribution: LLMs tuned with λ-GRPO outperform standard GRPO on reasoning tasks and reach peak performance more rapidly without explicit PRM or increased training cost.

problem: Theoretical analyses of ERM assume the Real-RAM model, but digital computation uses finite-precision hardware with finite-precision parameters and inputs.
approach: Analyzes ERM under a realistic bit-level model (ERM-bit) where parameters and inputs are rational numbers with polynomially bounded bit-lengths, revealing sharp tractability dichotomy based on activation function.
contribution: Shows piecewise-linear activations (ReLU) keep precision manageable and allow polynomial-time backpropagation, while polynomial activations with degree ≥2 make ERM-bit #P-hard, explaining ReLU's theoretical and practical success.

problem: Covariance matrix estimation typically relies on i.i.d. samples, but dependent samples from Markov chains are often more practical due to better query complexity.
approach: Investigates covariance estimation for Gibbs distributions based on dependent MCMC samples under Poincaré inequality and spectral gap conditions, establishing sample complexity bounds.
contribution: Shows MCMC can achieve similar sample complexity as i.i.d. estimators with potentially much better query complexity; provides improvements for constrained and unconstrained sampling on convex bodies.

problem: Evaluating mathematical reasoning in LLMs is constrained by limited benchmark sizes and high-variance accuracy estimates due to model stochasticity, yielding unstable rankings.
approach: Combines labeled outcomes with pairwise comparison signals from auxiliary reasoning chains as control variates, developing a semiparametric estimator based on the efficient influence function that achieves the semiparametric efficiency bound.
contribution: Substantially improves ranking accuracy and precision of performance estimation with gains increasing as model noise grows, demonstrated on GPQA Diamond, AIME 2025, and GSM8K.

problem: Optimal transport methods struggle to align distributions across heterogeneous domains while preserving geometric structure and remain computationally intractable in many settings.
approach: Convex Distance Operator Transport (CDOT) uses operator-based regularization that aligns aggregated distance structures via distance and conditional expectation operators while maintaining convexity and valid pseudometric properties.
contribution: Achieves convexity while preserving geometry on attributed compact metric-measure spaces; derives non-asymptotic risk bounds and demonstrates better performance on point clouds, brain connectomes, and graph classification.

problem: Conditional independence testing is central to causal inference but untestable in many settings without additional assumptions; existing approaches rely on restrictive structural conditions.
approach: Explores representation learning on spectral representations derived from singular value decomposition of partial covariance operators, introducing a bi-level contrastive algorithm to learn these representations for CI testing.
contribution: Links representation learning error to test performance with asymptotic validity and power guarantees, offering a principled path toward scalable CI testing bridging kernel-based theory with modern representation learning.

problem: Learning from geometrically structured data requires capturing meaningful feature alignments in space, but GNNs are limited by message passing while Transformers ignore geometry.
approach: Vector Bundle Attention Transformer (VBA-Transformer) redefines attention as an intrinsic geometric operator by coupling base manifold coordinates with fiber feature vectors via vector bundle theory and principled parallel transport.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on single-cell RNA sequencing benchmarks (outperforming Transformers by 3–5%), demonstrates superior performance on spatial transcriptomics, and validates competitive accuracy on 3D point clouds.

problem: RL algorithms with PPO-Clip are limited by exploration collapse due to implicit Euclidean metric measurement that is geometrically inconsistent with policy space Riemannian manifold.
approach: Riemannian Isometric Policy Optimization (RIPO) guarantees isometric policy updates on the Riemannian manifold, effectively balancing exploration and exploitation with a favorable bias-variance trade-off.
contribution: Significantly surpasses existing LLM RL algorithms on seven competition-level benchmarks, achieving up to 60% improvement over GRPO on AIME24.

problem: Distinguishing LLM-generated text from human writing is critical yet difficult because LLMs train to write like humans, leaving a mark.
approach: Telescope Perplexity evaluates token repetition probability P(s_i | s_{1:i}), hypothesizing that LLMs develop an aversion to token repetition as a vestigial heuristic from early training.
contribution: Enables highly effective zero-shot LLM detection with state-of-the-art or competitive performance across diverse datasets and perturbation schemes with greater efficiency than other methods.

problem: Integrating new modalities into Video LLMs typically requires heavy modality-specific encoders or paired supervision, limiting scalability.
approach: V-LynX exploits the token interface (continuous manifold allowing visual tokens to operate as standalone entities) and employs a lightweight auxiliary pathway parallel to the frozen vision encoder, aligning attention responses and statistical distributions using unpaired unimodal datasets.
contribution: Achieves SOTA efficiency across audio-visual QA, 3D reasoning, high-frame-rate, and multi-view video understanding without paired supervision.

problem: Computing differential entropy of distributions known only up to a normalization constant is fundamental but challenging; existing methods like P-SVGD fail to scale to high dimensions.
approach: MET-SVGD extends P-SVGD by correcting invertibility assumptions, including the critical trace-of-Hessian term, and providing stable hyperparameter selection with global convergence guarantees.
contribution: Achieves up to 12× and 16× lower entropy estimation error than P-SVGD and existing SVGD baselines; on CIFAR-10 energy-based generation improves FID by 80.4% with 64× higher training stability.

problem: LVLMs typically use the same video processing pipeline for diverse tasks (summarizing a 2-hour movie vs. counting birds in a 15-second clip), wasting resources.
approach: Task-Aware Mechanism (TAM) is a hybrid-gated MoE vision tower that adapts frame count and resolution to query and video length via a compact 0.1B Inductor trained on TA-116K dataset to infer task types.
contribution: Achieves SOTA performance among models with comparable LLMs on most video benchmarks and remains competitive against stronger-LLM baselines.

problem: Trained deep learning models raise intellectual property and information security concerns, yet existing code clone detection is insufficient to measure model similarity.
approach: Characterizes model topology structurally via normalized computational graphs and at the weight level employs statistical similarity measurement without explicit parameter alignment.
contribution: First definition of model cloning with a method for model similarity detection; demonstrates accurate detection on synthetic model clone benchmark and real-world open-source models.

problem: Multi-agent RL suffers from partial observability and inefficient information exchange; prior communication approaches fail to transmit sufficient state information.
approach: LMAC leverages an LLM's reasoning to design a communication protocol enabling all agents to reconstruct the underlying state accurately and uniformly, iteratively refining via an explicit state-awareness criterion.
contribution: Improves state reconstruction across agents and yields substantial performance gains over prior communication baselines on diverse MARL benchmarks.

problem: Traditional robot co-design converges to a single configuration, missing flexibility from reconfiguration across heterogeneous environments, while existing reconfigurable robot designs require human-designed configurations.
approach: Learning to Reconfigure proposes a holistic pipeline with low-level specialized primitives via multi-tail architecture and a high-level scheduler that dynamically switches configurations based on task progress.
contribution: Outperforms single-robot baselines by 5.95× average progress and co-design algorithms by 9.81× average progress on locomotion tasks across walking, flying, and swimming.

problem: Modality translation is under-constrained as multiple cross-modal mappings yield the same marginals; most existing approaches require fully paired datasets.
approach: Proposes a diffusion-bridge framework that characterizes admissible solution space and restricts it via alignment constraints, treating paired supervision as optional rather than prerequisite.
contribution: Achieves near fully-paired quality with substantial relaxation in pairing requirements, and remains applicable in unpaired regime on synthetic and real modality translation benchmarks.

problem: LLMs struggle with graph reasoning due to limited context windows, unreliable numerical computation, and structural hallucinations when passively ingesting graph knowledge.
approach: GRASP shifts from passive ingestion to proactive agentic exploration via Neighbor Retrieval for on-demand probing and Code Interpreter as deterministic solver, using staged RL (GRPO) transitioning from visible to structure-blind environment.
contribution: 4B model achieves 53.06% average performance boost on multi-domain graph reasoning benchmarks, surpassing DeepSeek-V3.2 and generalizing to unseen tasks.

problem: Diffusion policies for robotic manipulation suffer from substantial inference latency due to iterative denoising, limiting control frequency in real-time closed-loop systems.
approach: STEP proposes a lightweight spatiotemporal consistency prediction mechanism to construct high-quality warm-start actions distributionally close to target actions and temporally consistent, with velocity-aware perturbation injection.
contribution: With 2 steps, STEP achieves 21.6% and 27.5% higher success rate than BRIDGER and DDIM on RoboMimic and real-world tasks respectively, with theoretical analysis ensuring convergence.
